package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"

	"github.com/punt-labs/beadle/internal/daemon"
)

func main() {
	signerEmail := os.Args[1]
	outPath := os.Args[2]

	cmd := &daemon.Command{
		Name:         "hello",
		Runner:       "claude",
		Mode:         "process",
		Prompt:       "say hello",
		OutputSchema: "text",
	}
	cmd.Budget.Rounds = 1

	canon, err := daemon.CanonicalCommandBytes(cmd)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	gpgCmd := exec.Command("gpg", "--batch", "--no-tty", "--local-user", signerEmail,
		"--detach-sign", "--armor", "--output", "-")
	gpgCmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(canon)
	var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
	gpgCmd.Stdout = &out
	gpgCmd.Stderr = &errBuf
	if err := gpgCmd.Run(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, errBuf.String())
		panic(err)
	}
	cmd.Signature = out.String()

	data, err := yaml.Marshal(cmd)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(outPath, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("wrote", outPath)
}
EOF
cd <repo>
GNUPGHOME=$(cat .tmp/daemon-verify/gnupghome-path.txt)
FPR=$(cat .tmp/daemon-verify/fpr.txt)
mkdir -p .tmp/daemon-verify/scenario-c-valid/.punt-labs/beadle/commands
GNUPGHOME="$GNUPGHOME" go run ./.tmp/daemon-verify/gen-signed owner-verify@example.com \
  .tmp/daemon-verify/scenario-c-valid/.punt-labs/beadle/commands/hello.yaml
cat > .tmp/daemon-verify/scenario-c-valid/.punt-labs/beadle/daemon.json <<EOF
{"owner_gpg_key_id": "$FPR"}
EOF
echo "--- daemon.json ---"
cat .tmp/daemon-verify/scenario-c-valid/.punt-labs/beadle/daemon.json

tool_input.command:
cd <repo>
gh pr create --repo punt-labs/beadle --title "fix(daemon): wire VerifySignature into the command loader (DES-035)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Closes beadle-iru end to end. `VerifySignature` (DES-034, PR #251) had zero
callers at merge — the "zero agent authority" invariant existed in code but
was unenforced. This PR wires it into `beadle-daemon`'s command-file loader
so a configured daemon actually rejects unsigned or tampered command files.

- New `internal/daemon.Config` (`~/.punt-labs/beadle/daemon.json`) names the
  owner key via `owner_handle` (resolved through ethos) or
  `owner_gpg_key_id` (a direct 40-hex fingerprint, no-ethos path). Setting
  both is rejected as ambiguous.
- `LoadCommands`/`loadCommand` call `VerifySignature` before
  `validateCommand`, gated on `ownerKeyID != ""` — an unconfigured daemon
  has zero behavior change.
- **A `daemon.json` that is present but unresolvable (ambiguous config, bad
  handle, malformed fingerprint) disables command loading entirely** —
  `daemon.LoadCommands` is never even called — never falls back to loading
  commands unverified. Only a genuinely absent `daemon.json` keeps today's
  legacy unverified-loading behavior.
- `LoadCommands` now takes the daemon's own configured `*slog.Logger`, so a
  rejected command file's Error line persists to
  `~/.punt-labs/beadle/logs/beadle-daemon.log`, not just stderr.
- A distinct Error-level log line separates an operational verification
  failure (e.g. a broken `gpg` binary) from a genuine signature rejection
  and from an ordinary parse error.
- Neither mail polling nor the MCP server (a separate binary) depend on the
  commands map, so a misconfiguration disables command loading only, never
  the daemon process.
- Enforcement is opt-in until an operator configures `daemon.json`; there is
  no `beadle init`/`sign` onboarding flow yet, tracked as follow-on scope.

This PR includes a mid-flight process correction: the first local-review
round (code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter, type-design-analyzer) caught a
critical fail-open bug — a misconfigured `daemon.json` was silently
disabling *verification* while still loading every command file, the exact
backdoor DES-034/DES-035 exist to close. That was fixed in a follow-up
mission (bwk, evaluated by djb), then the full diff was re-reviewed clean.

## Design

`docs/wire-verifysignature.md` (DES-035), `DESIGN.md`'s DES-035 ADR entry.

## Test plan

- `make check` green: golangci-lint (0 issues), govulncheck (clean),
  `go test -race -count=1 ./...` (all packages green), markdownlint (0
  errors).
- Full-diff local review: `code-reviewer`, `silent-failure-hunter`,
  `type-design-analyzer` — two rounds, zero material findings on the
  second pass.
- **Real-entry-point verification** — built `beadle-daemon` and ran it
  (`beadle-daemon run`) against three isolated fake-`HOME` scenarios,
  expected output written down before running, compared against actual:
  - **Unconfigured** (no `daemon.json`): `signature_enforcement=false`,
    one unsigned command loads, no Error logged. Matched.
  - **Misconfigured** (`daemon.json` present, malformed fingerprint): Error
    "signature policy unavailable, command loading disabled" + Warn
    "command loading disabled", `count=0` — the same unsigned command that
    loaded in scenario 1 does **not** load, proving `LoadCommands` was
    never invoked. Matched — this is the fail-open bug's regression case,
    confirmed closed against the real binary, not just unit tests.
  - **Valid enforcement** (`daemon.json` with a real, resolvable
    fingerprint, one GPG-signed command + one unsigned sibling):
    `signature_enforcement=true`, signed command loads, unsigned sibling
    rejected with `reason=missing`, and the rejection line confirmed
    present in `~/.punt-labs/beadle/logs/beadle-daemon.log` (not just
    stderr).
- Bead beadle-iru closed with the full closure rationale.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1
